key_insight: The paper shows that entanglement entropy and magic can be estimated directly from ZX-diagrams by exploiting a normal form that separates a graph-state backbone from non-Clifford Pauli gadgets.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable resource diagnostics for large quantum circuits without expensive tensor contraction, useful for analyzing simulation cost, circuit complexity, and many-body behavior.
method: Use ZX flow to extract a normal form with an entangled graph-state backbone plus non-Clifford gadgets.
Derive additive upper and lower bounds on bipartite entanglement entropy from this structure.
Preprocess diagrams to remove or merge redundant non-Clifford contributions and obtain tighter bounds; also bound logarithmic stabilizer extent.
evidence_signal: The methods were benchmarked on random unitary circuits, monitored circuits, and Trotterized Hamiltonian evolution with Clifford layers, and the bounds stayed informative at large qubit counts, depths, and spider counts.
watch_item: The approach provides bounds rather than exact entanglement or magic values, so tightness may vary depending on diagram structure and the amount of preprocessing possible.
paper_title: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
